title: Two Sum
description:
Given an array of integers `nums` and an integer `target`, return indices of the two numbers such that they add up to `target`.

You may assume that each input would have exactly one solution, and you may not use the same element twice.

You can return the answer in any order.
constraints:
`2 <= nums.length <= 10^4`
`-10^9 <= nums[i] <= 10^9`
`-10^9 <= target <= 10^9`
Only one valid answer exists.
inputFormat:
Line 1: A comma-separated list of integers representing `nums`.
Line 2: An integer representing `target`.
outputFormat: A JSON array representing indices `[index1, index2]`.
hints: A really brute force way would be to search for all possible pairs, but that is O(N^2). Can you do better?
Try using a Hash Map to store complement values for O(N) lookup time!

title: Reverse String
description:
Write a function that reverses a string. The input string is given as an array of characters `s`.

You must do this by modifying the input array in-place with O(1) extra memory.
constraints:
`1 <= s.length <= 10^5`
`s[i]` is a printable ascii character.
inputFormat: A space-separated list of characters representing `s`.
outputFormat: The reversed array as a space-separated string of characters.
hints: Use a two-pointer approach starting from the ends of the array.
Swap the elements at the pointers and move inward until they meet.

starterCode.code:
import sys

def reverseString(s):
    # Modify s in-place
    l, r = 0, len(s) - 1
    while l < r:
        s[l], s[r] = s[r], s[l]
        l += 1; r -= 1

# --- Driver Code ---
if __name__ == '__main__':
    text = sys.stdin.read().strip()
    if text:
        s = text.split(' ')
        reverseString(s)
        print(' '.join(s))

title: Reverse Linked List
description: Given the head of a singly linked list, reverse the list, and return the reversed list (represented as comma-separated integers).
outputFormat: Comma-separated integer values of reversed nodes.
hints: Reverse iteratively or recursively.
Adjust node pointers in a loop.

title: Validate Binary Search Tree
description:
Given the root of a binary tree, determine if it is a valid binary search tree (BST).

A valid BST is defined as follows:
1. The left subtree of a node contains only nodes with keys less than the node's key.
2. The right subtree of a node contains only nodes with keys greater than the node's key.
3. Both the left and right subtrees must also be binary search trees.
constraints:
Number of nodes in tree is in range `[1, 10^4]`.
`-2^31 <= Node.val <= 2^31 - 1`
inputFormat: Comma-separated level-order tree representation where 'null' represents empty node.
explanation: Root node is 2. Left child 1 is less than 2. Right child 3 is greater than 2.
hints: For a node to be valid, all of its left children must be less, and right children must be greater.
Pass a range of allowed values [min, max] down the recursive stack.

title: Number of Islands
description:
Given an `m x n` 2D binary grid `grid` which represents a map of '1's (land) and '0's (water), return the number of islands.

An island is surrounded by water and is formed by connecting adjacent lands horizontally or vertically. You may assume all four edges of the grid are all surrounded by water.
constraints:
`m == grid.length`, `n == grid[i].length`
`1 <= m, n <= 300`
`grid[i][j]` is '0' or '1'.
inputFormat: JSON 2D grid of '0' and '1' string characters.
explanation: Grid has 3 islands separated by water.
hints: Run a DFS or BFS traversal whenever you hit a '1'.
Mark land nodes as visited (or convert to '0') to avoid processing again.

title: Coin Change
description:
You are given an integer array `coins` representing coins of different denominations and an integer `amount` representing a total amount of money.

Return the fewest number of coins that you need to make up that amount. If that amount of money cannot be made up by any combination of the coins, return `-1`.

You may assume that you have an infinite number of each kind of coin.
inputFormat:
Line 1: Comma-separated list of coins.
Line 2: The integer amount.
hints: Use a dynamic programming table dp[i] representing minimal coins for amount i.
For each coin, update dp[i] = min(dp[i], dp[i - coin] + 1).

title: Climbing Stairs (Recursion)
description: Calculate distinct climbing ways for `n` steps recursively.
hints: Climb from either step n-1 or n-2.

title: Jump Game
description:
Given an integer array `nums`, you are initially positioned at the array's first index. Each element in the array represents your maximum jump length at that position.

Return `true` if you can reach the last index, or `false` otherwise.
explanation: Jump 1 step from index 0 to 1, then 3 steps to the last index.
hints: Work backwards from the goal or trace the furthest index reachable at each step.

title: Valid Parentheses Stack
description: Determine if input string containing brackets is valid using a stack.
hints: Push open bracket to stack. Pop and check compatibility when you see close bracket.

title: Implement Queue using Array
description: Implement standard FIFO queue operations (push, pop, peek, empty) using an array.
explanation: Enqueue 1, enqueue 2. Peek gets front (1). Dequeue returns 1. Queue is not empty.
hints: Queue is FIFO: First In First Out.

title: Binary Search Index
description: Find index of target in sorted comma-separated integer array in O(log N).
inputFormat:
Line 1: Comma-separated sorted integers.
Line 2: Target integer.
hints: Compare target with midpoint, shrink search range in half.

title: Subsets Generator
description:
Given an integer array `nums` of unique elements, return all possible subsets (the power set).

The solution set must not contain duplicate subsets. Return the solution in any order.
outputFormat: JSON 2D array of all subsets sorted internally for validation.
hints: Use backtracking to branch between including or excluding each element.

title: Single Number Bits
description:
Given a non-empty array of integers `nums`, every element appears twice except for one. Find that single one.

You must implement a solution with a linear runtime complexity and use only constant extra space.
hints: XOR of any number with itself is 0, and with 0 is the number itself.
XOR all elements together.

title: Select High Earning Employees
description: Given an employee record table where each record contains `id`, `name`, and `salary`, retrieve a list of names of employees who earn more than `50000`.
constraints: Valid JSON employees list string input.
explanation: Alice earns 60000 which is > 50000, Bob earns 45000 which is not.
hints: Filter employees using where or list filter in JS/Python.

explanation: Words sorted alphabetically, each followed by count.
hints: Use a hashmap to count word frequencies, then sort alphabetically.

cat file.txt | tr -s ' ' '\n' | sort | uniq -c

title: Concurrency Coordinator Sequence
description: Design a sync structure guaranteeing three tasks execute in sequential order (First, Second, Third) regardless of scheduler thread choices.
explanation: Guarantees tasks run in perfect sequence.
hints: Use promises, async/await, or locks depending on language choice.

title: Deep Copy Javascript Object
description: Implement a full recursive deep clone utility in Javascript that creates a completely independent copy of a nested object or array, ensuring no reference links remain.
explanation: Deep copy has identical contents but different memory reference.
hints: Use recursion to check fields. If object, recursively copy. Avoid simple assignment.

title: Pandas DataFrame Query
description: Emulate the pandas dataframe filter operation `df[(df['A'] > 10) & (df['B'] < 5)]`. Given a dataset of rows containing integers A and B, return only rows that satisfy the criteria.
explanation: Row 1 (A=12, B=3) satisfies A > 10 and B < 5. Row 2 fails A > 10. Row 3 fails B < 5.
hints: In Python, you can use simple list comprehensions or lambda filters.
